samf-junior-2008-r1-02.title: Round
samf-junior-2008-r1-02.body:
$2008\approx2000$, $1710\approx1700$ and $3421\approx3400$, so the value is about $\frac{2000\times1700}{3400}=1000$. (Notice $3421\approx2\times1710$, so the value is about $\frac{2008}{2}\approx1004$.)

**Answer: (E) 1000**

samf-junior-2008-r1-05.title: Use the LCM
samf-junior-2008-r1-05.body:
A number divisible by 6 and 9 is divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,9)=18$. The multiples of 18 between 100 and 500 run from $6\times18=108$ to $27\times18=486$, which is $27-6+1=22$ numbers.

**Answer: (D) 22**

samf-junior-2008-r1-06.title: Count by the base
samf-junior-2008-r1-06.body:
Five lines meet at the top vertex (the vertical side, three inner lines and the hypotenuse). Triangles whose base is on the bottom line: choose 2 of the 5 lines, $\binom52=10$. Triangles whose base is on the short horizontal segment: it meets the vertical side and the next three lines, so choose 2 of these 4 lines, $\binom42=6$.

Total $10+6=16$.

**Answer: (B) 16**

samf-junior-2008-r1-07.title: Replace the protractors
samf-junior-2008-r1-07.body:
Five protractors cost the same as 7 set squares, so 5 protractors and 1 set square cost the same as 8 set squares: $8s=62$, $s=7.75$. Then $28s=28\times7.75=217$.

**Answer: (C) R217**

samf-junior-2008-r1-08.title: Common divisor
samf-junior-2008-r1-08.body:
The number of girls divides both 150 and 105. $150=2\cdot3\cdot5^2$ and $105=3\cdot5\cdot7$, so the greatest common divisor is $3\cdot5=15$.

**Answer: (D) 15**

samf-junior-2008-r1-10.title: List the splits
samf-junior-2008-r1-10.body:
The set can be split into two pairs in only 3 ways, each giving one positive difference:

- $\{16,13\}$ and $\{10,8\}$: $29-18=11$
- $\{16,10\}$ and $\{13,8\}$: $26-21=5$
- $\{16,8\}$ and $\{13,10\}$: $24-23=1$

There are 3 different positive answers.

**Answer: (E) 3**

samf-junior-2008-r1-11.title: Express everything in terms of a

samf-junior-2008-r1-12.title: Ratio parts
samf-junior-2008-r1-12.body:
The difference of $5-2=3$ parts is R600, so one part is R200. The total is $7$ parts $=7\times200=\text{R}1400$.

**Answer: (C) R1400**

samf-junior-2008-r1-13.title: Set up equations
samf-junior-2008-r1-13.body:
Let the number be $10x+y$. The new number is $100x+50+y$. Their difference is $90x+50=410$, so $x=4$. Digit sum: $4+5+y=12$ gives $y=3$. The number is 43 (and $453-43=410$). The difference of its digits is $4-3=1$.

**Answer: (B) 1**

samf-junior-2008-r1-14.title: Group in pairs
samf-junior-2008-r1-14.body:
Each pair $(399-397),(395-393),\ldots,(83-81)$ equals 2. The odd numbers from 81 to 399 number $\frac{399-81}{2}+1=160$, so there are $80$ pairs. The sum is $80\times2=160$.

**Answer: (D) 160**

samf-junior-2008-r1-15.title: Count factors of 2 and 5
samf-junior-2008-r1-15.body:
Six zeros need $2^6\cdot5^6$. In $16\cdot34\cdot75\cdot21\cdot13$ we have $16=2^4$, $34=2\cdot17$, $75=3\cdot5^2$: that is $2^5$ and $5^2$. So $n$ must supply at least one more 2 and four more 5s: $n=2\cdot5^4=1250$.

**Answer: (C) 1250**

samf-junior-2008-r1-16.title: Telescoping product
samf-junior-2008-r1-16.body:
$\left(1-\frac1k\right)=\frac{k-1}{k}$, so the product is $\frac45\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac67\cdots\frac{399}{400}=\frac4{400}=\frac1{100}$. Its square root is $\frac1{10}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac1{10}$**

samf-junior-2008-r1-17.title: Try both orientations
samf-junior-2008-r1-17.body:
All tiles must point the same way.

- 25 cm along the 710 side: $\lfloor710/25\rfloor=28$; 20 cm along 430: $\lfloor430/20\rfloor=21$; total $28\times21=588$.
- 20 cm along the 710 side: $\lfloor710/20\rfloor=35$; 25 cm along 430: $\lfloor430/25\rfloor=17$; total $35\times17=595$.

The maximum is 595.

**Answer: (C) 595**

samf-junior-2008-r1-18.title: Pattern of middle numbers
samf-junior-2008-r1-18.body:
The rows hold the odd numbers, with row $k$ containing $2k-1$ of them. The middle numbers are $1,5,13,25,\ldots=0^2+1^2,\,1^2+2^2,\,2^2+3^2,\,3^2+4^2$, so row $k$ has middle $(k-1)^2+k^2$.

For $k=61$: $60^2+61^2=3600+3721=7321$.

**Answer: (C) 7321**

samf-junior-2008-r1-18.title: Count the odd numbers
samf-junior-2008-r1-18.body:
The first 60 rows contain $1+3+\cdots+119=60^2=3600$ odd numbers. The middle of row 61 is the $3600+61=3661$st odd number, which is $2\times3661-1=7321$.

**Answer: (C) 7321**

samf-junior-2008-r1-19.title: Find the digit pattern
samf-junior-2008-r1-19.body:
$65^2=4225$, $665^2=442225$, $6665^2=44422225$. Each extra 6 in $x$ adds one 4 and one 2 to $x^2$, so the digit sum rises by 6. With $s$ sixes, $\#[x^2]=7+6s$.

$7+6s=49$ gives $s=7$, so $x=66\,666\,665$ (seven 6s then a 5).

**Answer: (D) 66 666 665**

samf-junior-2008-r1-20.title: Opposite faces
samf-junior-2008-r1-20.body:
In the strip of four squares, diamond and heart are opposite, and club and smiley are opposite. The two end squares (euro above the smiley and spade below the diamond) are the top and bottom, so euro and spade are opposite.

Cube (1) shows heart and diamond together, cube (2) shows spade and euro together, and cube (4) shows club and smiley together: each is impossible. Cubes (3) and (5) show three mutually adjacent faces and the clockwise order of the faces around the corner agrees with the net, so they can be obtained.

So exactly cubes (1), (2) and (4) cannot be obtained.

**Answer: (D)**
